attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: 'Can help' is a firm present-tense statement about what the tools can do, not a hedge about likelihood. The 'maybe even a new programming language' part is hedged and is kept as hedged, so it is not scored. The normalised proposition matches the statement.

contract.note: The plain reading (practical help learning to use an unfamiliar API, with no promise of mastery) is an ordinary, fair reading. It treats the language clause as tentative and does not set an arbitrary lower date cutoff.

evidence.note: Barke et al. preprint (2022), before the post date. A participant who was unsure of plt.hist's arguments got them from Copilot's suggestions and checked them against the docs. That is help discovering how to use an API. It is thin and does not isolate Copilot's share from the docs.

CHI 2022 abstract: users had trouble understanding Copilot's code. This limits any claim that the help is reliable, but it does not show that help with unfamiliar APIs is impossible. Counterevidence only.

reviews.rationale: The firm claim is that AI coding tools 'can help' a coder learn a new API. A pre-2025 observational study (e1) documents a participant getting unfamiliar API arguments from Copilot and confirming them, which is practical help discovering API usage. The comprehension problems in e2 limit reliability but do not defeat 'can help'. The hedged programming-language clause is not scored.
